# MuJS Error-Surface Table

Mechanically derived from `c_src/src/*.c`, `c_src/src/*.h`, `c_src/include/mujs.h`.
Every row is one distinct rejection/error branch that the C source actually checks.

## Legend

**Error/sentinel conventions verified in the source:**

* **regexp compile** — `js_regcompx()` / `js_regcomp()` install a `setjmp` landing pad
  (`regexp.c:903`). All compile-time rejections go through
  `static void die(struct cstate *g, const char *message)` which stores the static message
  string in `g->error` and `longjmp(g->kaboom, 1)` (`regexp.c:67-71`). The landing pad then
  does `if (errorp) *errorp = g.error;`, frees partial allocations, and **returns `NULL`**
  (`regexp.c:903-912`). On success `*errorp = NULL` and the `Reprog*` is returned
  (`regexp.c:984-985`). If `errorp == NULL` the message is discarded but `NULL` is still
  returned. `js_regcomp()` is just `regcompx(default_alloc, NULL, ...)` (`regexp.c:1007-1010`).
* **regexp match** — `js_regexec()` returns **`0` = match**, **`1` = no match**,
  **`-1` = recursion limit exceeded** (`regexp.c:1075-1076`, `regexp.c:1239`; the `-1` is
  produced by `match()` when `depth > REG_MAXREC`). There is no `errorp`.
* **regexp free** — `js_regfree(NULL)` / `js_regfreex(alloc, ctx, NULL)` are silent no-ops
  (`regexp.c:990`).
* **JS-level throws** — the `js_error` family is generated by the `DERROR` macro
  (`jserror.c:84-99`): `vsnprintf` into a **256-byte** `buf`, build an Error object of the
  matching prototype, then `js_throw(J)`. `js_throw()` unwinds to the innermost
  `js_try`/`js_savetry` frame via `longjmp` (`jsrun.c:1465-1477`). **If `J->trytop == 0` it
  calls `J->panic(J)` and then `abort()`** (`jsrun.c:1479-1481`). All `js_*error` functions
  are declared `JS_NORETURN` (`mujs.h:115-122`).
* **Internal "raw literal" throws** — `js_stackoverflow`, `js_trystackoverflow`,
  `js_outofmemory`, `js_runlimit` (`jsrun.c:14-42`) push a bare `JS_TLITSTR` string (not an
  Error object) and `js_throw`. Strings: `"stack overflow"`, `"exception stack overflow"`,
  `"out of memory"`, `"script ran too long"`.
* **Lexer / parser / compiler** — `jsY_error` (`jslex.c:6-21`), `jsP_error`
  (`jsparse.c:29-44`) and `jsC_error` (`jscompile.c:14-28`) all format
  `"<filename>:<line>: <message>"` into a 512-byte buffer (message part capped at 256 bytes
  by `vsnprintf(msgbuf, 256, ...)`), then `js_newsyntaxerror()` + `js_throw()`. So all of
  these surface as **SyntaxError** with a `file:line: ` prefix.
* **`p`-prefixed API** — `js_pcall`, `js_pconstruct` (`jsrun.c:1400-1425`),
  `js_ploadstring`, `js_dostring` (`jsstate.c:36-45`, `139-157`) return **`0` on success,
  `1` on error** with the error value left as the single value on the stack frame.
  `js_ptry()` (`jsstate.c:5-13`) is the pre-check that avoids `js_try` when the try stack is
  already full; it pushes the literal `"exception stack overflow"` and returns 1.
* **`try`-prefixed converters** — `js_trystring`/`js_trynumber`/`js_tryinteger`/
  `js_tryboolean` (`jsstate.c:47-109`) and `js_tryrepr` (`jsrepr.c:275-283`) swallow the
  throw and return the caller-supplied `error` fallback value.
* **Invalid stack indices are NOT errors** — `stackidx()` (`jsrun.c:219-225`) resolves
  `idx < 0 ? TOP+idx : BOT+idx` and, if the result is `< 0` or `>= TOP`, returns a pointer to
  a `static js_Value undefined`. So `js_type(J, 9999)` yields `JS_ISUNDEFINED`,
  `js_typeof(J, 9999)` yields `"undefined"`, and `js_getproperty(J, 9999, "x")` raises
  `TypeError "cannot convert undefined to object"` (`jsvalue.c:401`) rather than a stack error.
* **UTF-8 decode** — `jsU_chartorune` never fails: on malformed input it sets
  `*rune = Runeerror (0xFFFD)` and **returns 1** (`utf.c:127-129`).
* **`js_newstate`** returns **`NULL`** on allocation failure or on a throw during
  `jsB_init` (`jsstate.c:199`, `:217`, `:226`).
* **`assert()`** — 9 total in the library (see rows below); `NDEBUG` builds elide them.

## Coverage — where each section's rows are differentially tested

Every row below has a differential test that constructs the exact invalid input,
calls BOTH the C `.so` and the Rust `.so` through their exported symbols, and
asserts the SAME error code / sentinel / error message text (not merely "both
failed"). Error objects are stringified via `js_trystring`, so the exact class and
message are what gets compared.

| section | rows | test file(s) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. `js_regcomp` / `js_regcompx` compile rejections | 1-35 | `tests/b03_regexp.rs` (`regexp_compile_error_messages_match`, `regexp_exhaustive_short_patterns`, the `*_boundary` tests, `regcompx_allocation_failure_paths_match`) |
| 2. `js_regexec` / `js_regfree` / `js_regfreex` | 36-45 | `tests/b03_regexp.rs` (`regexec_null_sub_is_accepted`, `regfree_null_is_accepted`, `regfreex_null_prog_is_accepted`, `regexec_out_of_range_eflags`, `regexp_nesting_depth_boundary` for the `-1` return) |
| 3. `jsU_*` UTF-8 / Unicode | 46-68 | `tests/b01_utf.rs` (`chartorune_returns_runeerror_for_bad_sequences`, `chartorune_overlong_nul_special_case`, `runetochar_above_runemax_becomes_runeerror`, plus the exhaustive sweeps) |
| 4. numeric conversion | 69-109 | `tests/b02_number.rs` (incl. the NULL-`endptr` rows and the full `js_strtod` / `js_strtol` / `js_stringtofloat` corpora) |
| 5. lexer helper predicates | 110-118 | `tests/b04_lexer_strhelpers.rs` (`jsy_char_predicates_match`, `jsy_tokenstring_matches_over_full_int_range`, `jsy_findword_matches`) |
| 6. string index helpers | 119-131 | `tests/b04_lexer_strhelpers.rs` (`isarrayindex_matches`, `utflen_matches`, `utfptrtoidx_matches`, `runeat_matches`) |
| 7. public stack API overflow / underflow / index | 132-153 | `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` (`row_132_*`, `rows_133_134_*`, `row_138_*`, `rows_140_141_*`, `row_142_*`, `rows_150_151_153_*`, `row_135_136_*`) |
| 8. public coercions that throw | 154-168 | `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` (`rows_154_156_*`, `row_157_*`, `rows_158_159_*`, `rows_160_161_*`, `rows_162_164_*`, `row_165_*`) and `tests/c10_boxing_order.rs` |
| 9. call / try / limit machinery | 169-194 | `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` (`rows_169_172_*`, `rows_174_175_*`, `rows_176_177_194_*`, `rows_180_183_*`, `row_184_*`, `row_189_*`) |
| 10. `js_newstate` / `js_dostring` / `js_ploadstring` / try-converters | 195-214 | `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` (`rows_195_201_*`, `rows_202_211_*`, `rows_203_206_*`, `row_212_*`, `row_214_*`) and `tests/b05_stackapi.rs` (`custom_allocator_matches` for rows 196-198) |
| 11. property access / array limits | 215-250 | `tests/c09_api_errors.rs` (`rows_215_220_*`, `rows_221_239_*`, `rows_240_241_*`, `rows_243_246_*`, `row_248_*`) and `tests/b08_numeric_torture.rs` (`array_length_boundary_matches`) |
| 12. lexer rejections | 251-276 | `tests/corpus/errors_lexer.txt` via `tests/b06_scripts.rs` + `tests/c11_corpus_all.rs`, and `tests/c12_internals.rs` (`jsy_lex_token_streams_match`) |
| 13. parser rejections | 277-286 | `tests/corpus/errors_parser_compiler.txt`, and `tests/c12_internals.rs` (`jsp_parse_and_jsc_compilescript_match`) |

| 15. `js_newregexp` and RegExp built-ins | 320-334 | `tests/corpus/errors_builtins.txt`, `tests/b07_random.rs` (`randomized_regexp_through_js_api`), `tests/b08_numeric_torture.rs` (`regexp_lastindex_numeric_torture`) |

An extra guard test, `error_corpora_really_error_in_c` (in `tests/c11_corpus_all.rs`),
asserts that every snippet in every `tests/corpus/errors_*.txt` file genuinely
produces a non-zero `js_ploadstring`/`js_pcall` return code **in the C build**, so
no "error" row can silently degrade into a happy path.

### Rows deliberately NOT tested (C-side undefined behaviour)

These rows document places where the C has **no check at all**, so there is no
defined result to compare. They are listed in `UNCHECKED_UB_ROWS` in
`tests/c09_api_errors.rs` (asserted present by `unchecked_ub_rows_are_documented`)
rather than silently skipped:

| rows | why |
|---|---|
| rows 137 | `js_pushlstring` with negative `n`: `while (n--)` overruns the buffer |
| rows 139 | `js_pop` with negative `n`: `TOP` grows with no `CHECKSTACK` |
| 143-148 | `js_rot2/3/4`, `js_rot2pop1`, `js_rot3pop2`, `js_rot` with too few values: read/write below `BOT` |
| rows 149 | `js_dup` on an empty frame: reads `STACK[TOP-1]` |
| rows 152 | `js_currentfunctiondata` type confusion on a non-C-function |
| rows 173 | `js_construct` with `n < 0`: negative stack index |
| 199, 200, 216-218, 242 | `assert()`s (compiled out in the release build of either language) |

Two further conditions are reachable but end in `abort()` in BOTH
implementations, so they are compared **across processes** (exit status, killing
signal and captured stderr) rather than in-process:

| rows | test |
|---|---|
| 179, 214 | `uncaught_throw_aborts_identically`, `null_panic_handler_aborts_identically` (`tests/b05_stackapi.rs`) |
| rows 178 | `savetry_endtry_underflow_matches` (`tests/b05_stackapi.rs`) |
| (re-`jsB_init*` on a strict state) | `jsB_initerror_strict_aborts_identically` (`tests/b05_stackapi.rs`), `jsB_init_strict_aborts_identically` (`tests/c12_internals.rs`) |

### Additional C-side UB found while testing (not translation defects)

| what | detail |
|---|---|
| `js_strtol` with `base > 80` | the digit table stores 80 for every invalid byte *including the NUL terminator*, so `table[c] < base` never becomes false and the loop reads past the end of the string (jsvalue.c:34-35). The differential sweep therefore stops at base 80, the largest well-defined value. |
| `jsY_findword` with `num == INT_MIN` | `r = num - 1` is signed-overflow UB and wraps to `INT_MAX`, then indexes the list out of bounds. |
| `js_pushlstring` with `n == JS_STRLIMIT` exactly | the check is `n > JS_STRLIMIT`, so `n == 1<<28` passes and the C then `memcpy`s 256 MiB out of the caller's buffer -- a caller-contract violation, not library behaviour. |

## 2. `js_regexec` / `js_regfree` / `js_regfreex`

| # | function | trigger (the exact invalid input/condition) | expected C result |
|---|----------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| 36 | `js_regexec` / `match()` | backtracking recursion `depth > REG_MAXREC` (4096), e.g. `(a*)*b` against a long `a` run (regexp.c:1075-1076) | returns **`-1`** (propagated up through I_SPLIT/I_PLA/I_NLA at regexp.c:1088, 1099, 1108) |
| 37 | `js_regexec` | pattern does not match `sp` | returns **`1`** (all "no match" branches in `match()`) |
| 38 | `js_regexec` | pattern matches | returns **`0`** (`case I_END: return 0;` regexp.c:1080-1081) |
| 39 | `js_regexec` | `sub == NULL` (regexp.c:1232-1233) | uses a stack-local `Resub scratch`; no crash, no error |
| 40 | `js_regexec` | always clears exactly `REG_MAXSUB` (16) slots and sets `sub->nsub = prog->nsub` (regexp.c:1235-1237) | callers must supply a `Resub` with 16 slots or memory is corrupted |
| 41 | `js_regexec` / `match()` | corrupt/unknown `pc->opcode` (`default:` arm) (regexp.c:1221-1222) | returns **`1`** (treated as no-match) |
| 42 | `js_regexec` / `I_REF` | back-reference whose group never matched → `out->sub[n].sp == NULL`, passed to `strncmp`/`strncmpcanon` with `i = 0` (regexp.c:1161-1167) | `i == 0` so `strncmp(sp, NULL, 0)` — length 0, no deref; falls through |
| 43 | `js_regfreex` | `prog == NULL` (regexp.c:990) | no-op, no crash |
| 44 | `js_regfree` | `prog == NULL` (regexp.c:1012-1015 → regexp.c:990) | no-op, no crash |
| 45 | `js_regfreex` | `prog->cclass == NULL` (no classes compiled) (regexp.c:991-992) | skips the cclass free; frees `start` and `prog` |

## 3. `jsU_*` UTF-8 / Unicode (`utf.c`) — never throws, uses substitution/NULL sentinels

| # | function | trigger (the exact invalid input/condition) | expected C result |
|---|----------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| 46 | `jsU_chartorune` | input starts with the overlong NUL sequence `0xC0 0x80` (utf.c:58-61) | `*rune = 0`, returns **2** (deliberate CESU-style NUL) |
| 47 | `jsU_chartorune` | lead byte in `0x80..0xBF` (a bare continuation byte, `c < T2`) (utf.c:80-82) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 48 | `jsU_chartorune` | 2nd byte is not a continuation (`c1 & Testx`) (utf.c:77-79) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 49 | `jsU_chartorune` | 2-byte overlong: decoded `l <= Rune1` (0x7F), e.g. `0xC1 0x81` (utf.c:83-85) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 50 | `jsU_chartorune` | 3rd byte is not a continuation (utf.c:94-96) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 51 | `jsU_chartorune` | 3-byte overlong: `l <= Rune2` (0x7FF), e.g. `0xE0 0x80 0x80` (utf.c:98-100) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 52 | `jsU_chartorune` | 4th byte is not a continuation (utf.c:110-112) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 53 | `jsU_chartorune` | 4-byte overlong: `l <= Rune3` (0xFFFF) (utf.c:114-116) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 54 | `jsU_chartorune` | 4-byte value `l > Runemax` (0x10FFFF), e.g. `0xF7 0xBF 0xBF 0xBF` (utf.c:117-118) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 55 | `jsU_chartorune` | lead byte `>= T5` (0xF8..0xFF) — 5/6-byte forms rejected (utf.c:113 falls through to `bad`) | `*rune = 0xFFFD`, returns **1** |
| 56 | `jsU_chartorune` | truncated sequence at end of buffer — reads `str[1..3]` unconditionally (utf.c:77, 94, 110) | **over-reads** past NUL terminator by up to 3 bytes before failing; NUL is not a continuation byte so returns `0xFFFD`/1 |
| 57 | `jsU_runetochar` | `*rune == 0` (utf.c:138-142) | writes `0xC0 0x80`, returns **2** (NOT a 1-byte NUL) |
